body:
This report relates to activity observed in account 38-63800-1, held by Isadora Saltonstall at Cortex Bank and Trust, during a review period from February 19, 2024, through July 31, 2024. The total cash deposited into the subject account during this timeframe was $135,462.60. A review of this account was initiated following a branch referral noting the customer's inquiries regarding reporting thresholds at the teller line.

Subsequent analysis identified a pattern of transactions consistent with structuring for the purpose of evading the $10,000 Currency Transaction Report filing requirement. The activity observed was characterised by a series of cash deposits, frequently clustered in amounts between $5,937.87 and $5,688.37. The reviewing analyst noted branch rotation within a single business day on several occasions, further supporting the suspicion of structuring.

Other outbound payments also left the account, with the largest single outbound transfer during the review period being $148,388.97.

body: The determinative finding of this review is that the structuring activity conducted by Isadora Saltonstall was not an isolated attempt to conceal personal cash holdings, but part of a coordinated effort to fund an undisclosed corporate entity. While the initial analysis focused on the aggregate cash volume deposited during the review period, the reviewing analyst established that the sub-threshold cash deposits were systematically aggregated and subsequently moved via outbound transfers. Specifically, on July 16, 2024, a consolidation transfer of $38,212.37 was executed from account 38-63800-1, directed to an external account held by Mapleford Trading Inc., which was previously unknown to Cortex Bank and Trust. The reviewing analyst determined that the funds credited to the receiving account 11-80420-9 were entirely composed of the structured cash deposits made by the subject in the preceding weeks, indicating that the structuring was conducted with the express purpose of funding this entity while evading currency transaction reporting requirements.

The total value of the transactions reviewed during this period was $283,490.62. The activity under review was initially identified by the bank's automated transaction monitoring system, which generated alerts regarding potential exposure to a sanctioned jurisdiction.

A review of the transaction history indicated that the subject account received multiple incoming wire transfers and initiated outgoing payments that exhibited characteristics consistent with attempts to evade sanctions screening controls. The transactions involved counterparties including Bright Harbor Marine Services Inc., Marblehead Ventures Corp., and Falcon Crest Ventures Corp. The activity observed included instances where shipping documents appeared to be re-routed through a known transshipment hub, a common indicator of potential sanctions evasion. Furthermore, certain payment references were observed to have originator details removed. The investigation also identified a counterparty address located in a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction.

body:
This report describes activity identified by Cortex Bank and Trust during a review period from November 29, 2023, through April 8, 2024. The subject of this review is Greystone Ventures Enterprises LLC, maintaining Cortex Bank and Trust account 66-96376-1. The review was prompted by a branch referral following a customer contact regarding a suspected compromised communication channel resulting in an unauthorized funds transfer.

The identified activity involves a single outbound wire transfer totaling $3,827,497.24, initiated from the Greystone Ventures Enterprises LLC account. The transaction pattern is consistent with wire fraud, wherein funds were induced out of the customer account by deception and moved to a beneficiary not intended by the customer. The customer reported that the transfer instructions were received via email, later determined to have originated from a lookalike sender domain differing by one character from a known vendor's domain. The instructions included urgency language that circumvented the customer's established dual-approval control, and the beneficiary name on the transfer instructions did not match the name of the invoicing vendor.

body: The determinative finding of this review is that the subject's funds were systematically transferred to an unrelated third party through a series of structured transactions. Analysis of account 89-15385-9 at a correspondent institution revealed that a significant portion of the withdrawn funds ultimately benefited Cyrus Cromwell, an individual with no known familial or business relationship to the subject. body:
A review of activity within account 86-89538-1, held by Philippa Cromwell, was initiated following a branch referral received on March 1, 2024. The referring branch noted the customer asked specific, unprompted questions regarding the reporting requirements for large cash transactions while making a cash deposit. Subsequent analysis covered the period from January 4, 2024, through May 23, 2024. During this review period, Cortex Bank and Trust observed an aggregate cash volume deposited totaling $345,600.38. The activity was identified as potentially indicative of structuring to evade Currency Transaction Report requirements.

The review period captured a pattern of frequent cash deposits, primarily conducted in person at various Cortex Bank and Trust branch locations. The deposits were consistently sized just below the $10,000 threshold that triggers mandatory reporting. While the aggregate cash volume deposited during the review period was substantial, no individual cash deposit exceeded the reporting threshold. The pattern of deposits, characterized by their frequency and size, raised concerns regarding intentional avoidance of regulatory scrutiny.

body:

The review was initiated following an automated monitoring alert generated on March 25, 2024, which flagged an anomalous outbound wire transfer. The subsequent investigation identified a pattern of activity consistent with wire fraud, wherein funds appear to have been induced out of the customer account by deception and moved by wire to a beneficiary the customer did not intend to pay.

The reviewing analyst noted that the transaction occurred just minutes before the daily wire processing cutoff time, a timing anomaly often associated with attempts to limit the window for interception or recall. Further review of the payment instructions revealed discrepancies that warranted escalation.

body: The determinative finding of this review is that the fraudulent payment instructions were not executed in a single outbound wire, but rather that a substantial portion of the diverted funds was subsequently routed to an unrelated third party. The reviewing analyst established that on June 19, 2024, the receiving institution executed an onward transfer of $335,562.76 from their holding account 19-18057-9 to an account held by Highfield Commodities Group LLC. This onward transfer occurred prior to Cortex Bank and Trust's initial recall request and the subsequent freeze action by the receiving institution. No legitimate business relationship between Ephraim Balogun, the invoicing vendor, and the recipient of this onward transfer could be established, and the customer confirmed no prior dealings with this entity. The movement of these funds is consistent with an effort to rapidly distance the proceeds from the initial point of compromise.

body:
Upon confirmation of the fraudulent nature of the outbound wire transfer, Cortex Bank and Trust executed its incident response protocol to secure the customer account and mitigate further risk. On March 25, 2024, an immediate, total account freeze was placed on account 72-77209-1, held by Ephraim Balogun. This restriction disabled all transaction channels, including online banking access, automated clearing house origination, wire transfer capabilities, and debit card usage. The freeze was necessary to prevent any subsequent unauthorized funds movement while the investigation progressed and to secure the account from potential external compromise.

The relationship manager assigned to Ephraim Balogun was instructed to contact the customer and mandate an immediate password reset for all online banking credentials, along with a mandatory review of account security settings. The customer was further advised to conduct a comprehensive scan of their internal systems for malware or unauthorized access, given the suspicion that the fraudulent instructions originated from a compromised email account or internal system vulnerability.

body:
Granite Point Metals Trading Co. established a relationship with Cortex Bank and Trust by opening a commercial checking account, numbered 24-27345-1, on June 6, 2024. The account was opened by a relationship manager operating out of a branch location. The customer profile completed at onboarding indicated the entity was engaged in the domestic wholesale trade of industrial metals. The anticipated activity profile projected a low volume of high-value domestic wire transfers, with counterparties primarily expected to be established manufacturers and regional distributors. Based on the representations made during the onboarding process, the account was assigned a low risk rating. The initial funding was deposited on June 28, 2024, in the amount of $155,439.87.

The account was apparently opened under a documentary exception that permitted initial funding prior to the completion of all required verifications. This exception, however, was never cleared, leaving the source of the initial funds unverified.

body: Review of the due diligence file for Granite Point Metals Trading Co. revealed a critical documentary exception at onboarding that was never cleared, despite the account remaining active. The relationship manager approved the account opening on June 6, 2024, without securing required source-of-funds evidence for an initial funding amount of $155,439.87. Subsequent transaction analysis identified that the largest single transaction with no source-of-funds evidence was a wire transfer of $410,975.35 to Cornerstone Freight Group LLC on July 12, 2024. The determinative finding of this review is that on October 8, 2024, the reviewing analyst established that a total of $420,800.75 was attributable to Larkfield Exports Group LLC, an entity entirely omitted from the initial customer profile and beneficial ownership documentation. This sum was observed to have moved through account 42-34431-9, held at another institution and linked to the subject. The failure to clear the initial documentary exception allowed aggregate activity of $900,161.92 to occur without adequate CDD, rendering the low risk tier assigned to the account insupportable.

body:
This review of activity occurring between November 21, 2023, and May 6, 2024, was initiated following an automated monitoring alert concerning the activity of Quentin Underhill. The alert identified a pattern of cash deposits to Cortex Bank and Trust account 39-20818-1 that appeared designed to evade the $10,000 currency transaction reporting requirement. The aggregate cash volume deposited during the review period was $284,810.58. The reviewing analyst assessed the activity against the customer profile and identified significant deviations from expected account usage.

The investigation focused on the volume and velocity of cash deposits, which were consistently maintained below the regulatory reporting threshold. Initial findings indicated that the majority of these transactions were clustered in the high four figures. The customer utilized multiple branch locations, sometimes conducting transactions at different branches on the same business day. This behavior is consistent with attempts to obscure the total volume of cash being introduced into the financial system and to avoid triggering internal reporting mechanisms.

body:
On September 3, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust received a customer inquiry from Solveig Fontaine concerning an outbound wire transfer initiated from account 10-60575-1 on August 15, 2024. Fontaine stated that her established vendor had denied any link to the payee of the August 15 transfer. A preliminary review of the transaction details prompted a referral to the Financial Intelligence Unit for further investigation into suspected wire fraud. The review period for this investigation was established as May 27, 2024, through November 15, 2024, to capture the transaction in question and assess prior account activity for related anomalies.

The suspicious activity reviewed here began with an outgoing domestic wire transfer in the amount of $276,618.57, executed on August 15, 2024. The transfer was initiated via the online banking platform. The beneficiary of the transfer was recorded as Limestone Ventures Group LLC. The stated purpose of the wire, as entered in the online banking system, was invoice payment. The activity is consistent with a business email compromise scheme, wherein a spoofed vendor email deceives a customer into paying a purported affiliate of that vendor.

While the payment instructions indicated settlement for an invoice submitted by Cedarline Holdings Group LLC, the routing information directed the funds to a different entity entirely. Specifically, the reviewing analyst determined that the $404,038.31 transfer was not credited to Cedarline Holdings Group LLC, but instead was routed to an external account held by Xiomara Oyelaran. On August 27, 2024, the reviewing analyst placed a debit block on Cortex Bank and Trust account 10-60575-1, held by Solveig Fontaine. This action was taken to prevent further dissipation of funds following the identification of the outbound wire transfer to Limestone Ventures Group LLC. The block restricted all outgoing funds transfers, automated clearing house debits, and check clearing. Inbound credits were permitted to continue, allowing the account to receive potential returned funds.

Concurrent with the debit block, the reviewing analyst initiated an urgent recall request through the Fedwire system for the $276,618.57 transfer. Communication was established with the receiving institution to secure the funds. The receiving institution confirmed receipt of the recall request and subsequently notified Cortex Bank and Trust that a portion of the funds had been secured.

The receiving institution was able to freeze $24,895.67 in the beneficiary account. The remaining funds had already been withdrawn or transferred prior to the execution of the freeze order.

The alert identified patterns of cash deposits that appeared designed to circumvent Currency Transaction Report requirements. During the review period from March 1, 2024 through July 30, 2024, the account held by Elowen Oyelaran (13-66819-1) exhibited a pattern of cash deposits that appeared designed to circumvent the $10,000 regulatory reporting threshold. The aggregate cash volume deposited during this period reached $502,959.25. The reviewing analyst noted that these deposits were frequently clustered in amounts between $3,495.21 and $1,445.00. The timing and sequencing of these transactions, particularly the execution of multiple deposits on the same day across different branch locations, strongly indicated an intent to evade currency transaction reporting requirements.

The structural features of this activity were evident early in the review period. On March 1, 2024, a deposit of $9,080.01 was recorded at a branch location in the morning. Later that same day, a second deposit of $8,368.99 was executed at a different branch location. The total cash deposited on this date exceeded the $10,000 reporting threshold, yet neither individual transaction triggered a report. This branch rotation strategy, executed within a single business day, is a classic indicator of structuring.

The investigation focuses on whether these transactions represent an attempt to evade US economic sanctions by utilizing complex corporate structures or obscured routing.

body:
A grand jury subpoena from the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York was served on Cortex Bank and Trust on August 15, 2024. The subpoena compelled the production of all account records, signature cards, monthly statements, cancelled checks, deposit slips, wire transfer records, and correspondence pertaining to Dashiell Pemberton and account 81-23986-1. The subpoena specifically referenced Driftwood Logistics Partners LP, Lanternhill Trading Enterprises LLC, and Beacon Logistics LLC. Cortex Bank and Trust complied with the subpoena, providing the requested documentation to the designated Assistant United States Attorney.

Subsequent to the receipt of the subpoena, the reviewing analyst initiated information sharing under Section 314(b) of the USA PATRIOT Act. A request was transmitted to the institution holding the accounts for Driftwood Logistics Partners LP, Lanternhill Trading Enterprises LLC, and Beacon Logistics LLC. The request sought clarification on the nature of the relationship between Dashiell Pemberton and these entities, as well as the business purpose of the financial activity observed during the review period.

Outbound activity was similarly predictable, consisting almost entirely of scheduled electronic payments to the care facility and a small number of recurring utility and insurance payments.

The statistical baseline maintained by the transaction monitoring system reflected this stable pattern.

body:
A grand jury subpoena was received by Cortex Bank and Trust on June 20, 2023, compelling the production of account opening documents, signature cards, and transactional records for the account held by Ulises Vasquez. The subpoena, issued by the United States Attorney’s Office for the district in which the subject resides, requested records covering the period from June 20, 2023, through the date of production. The bank’s legal department coordinated the gathering and review of the requested documents. The production was completed and transmitted to the designated Assistant United States Attorney on July 14, 2023. The transmittal letter noted the account number, 37-89750-2, and confirmed that the production included all responsive records held by the bank.

A subsequent written request for information was received from a federal law enforcement agency on June 30, 2023. This request sought information regarding specific wire transfers originating from the account of Ulises Vasquez. The agency indicated an ongoing investigation into potential financial exploitation.

body:
This report details the findings of an investigation into account activity conducted by Marisol Wolcott through Cortex Bank and Trust account 30-60258-1. The review period for this investigation spans from June 15, 2023, through April 26, 2024. The investigation was initiated following an automated monitoring alert that identified a pattern of cash deposits indicative of potential structuring to evade the Currency Transaction Reporting threshold of $10,000. The activity under review primarily involves a series of sub-threshold cash deposits, followed by outbound transfers to various entities. The aggregate cash volume deposited during the review period totaled $291,990.01.

The investigation focuses on the nature and velocity of these cash deposits, which were consistently conducted in amounts just below the $10,000 reporting requirement. The timing and frequency of these deposits, coupled with the subsequent movement of funds out of the account, present a fact pattern consistent with attempts to obscure the origin and total volume of the cash being introduced into the financial system.

body: Anders Macallister established his relationship with Cortex Bank and Trust in the third quarter of 2021, opening checking account 68-99803-2. At onboarding, Macallister provided documentation identifying himself as a self-employed marine consultant and listed his primary residence in a coastal community within the bank's operational footprint. The customer profile completed at that time indicated expected monthly deposit activity in the low five figures, comprised almost exclusively of check deposits and electronic transfers originating from domestic commercial entities. The anticipated outgoing activity was described as routine household expenses and transfers to an external brokerage account. Based on the customer declaration and the absence of complex products, foreign entanglements, or cash-intensive anticipated activity, the relationship was assigned a standard risk rating at inception. This standard risk classification remained undisturbed through the first two annual periodic reviews, as the account activity largely mirrored the expected profile established at onboarding.

The primary account of concern in this investigation was opened at Cortex Bank and Trust by Kirsten Fitzgerald. The account, numbered 69-73140-3, is a standard personal checking product established several years prior to the events under review. Historical analysis indicates that the account was originally funded with a low four-figure sum, consistent with a typical retail checking account opening deposit. Throughout its history, prior to the review period, the account exhibited a highly predictable and unremarkable pattern of use, functioning primarily as a repository for periodic payroll deposits and a source for routine household expenditures.

Prior to the events that triggered this review, the typical monthly credit volume into account 69-73140-3 was generally confined to a narrow range of several thousand dollars. These credits were overwhelmingly electronic, consisting almost entirely of direct deposits from an employer, with occasional, small-value peer-to-peer transfers or minimal cash deposits that rarely exceeded a few hundred dollars.

The activity observed in Cortex Bank and Trust account 68-99803-2, held by Anders Macallister, exhibited geographic patterns that elevated the jurisdictional risk profile of the relationship. Analysis of the deposit locations during the review period ending April 26, 2024, identified significant branch rotation, a recognized indicator of potential structuring when coupled with cash deposits clustered just below the $10,000 currency transaction reporting threshold. The customer frequently utilized multiple, geographically dispersed Cortex Bank and Trust branches within a tight radius, often executing transactions at different locations on the same business day or consecutive days.

This pattern was particularly evident in the summer of 2023. A review of transaction records indicated that the customer did not rely on a primary branch near their residential address on file. Instead, the activity was spread across several branches in adjacent counties. This deliberate dispersion of activity across the branch network is inconsistent with typical retail banking behavior, where a customer generally favors convenience and proximity.

Following the receipt of this incident report, the assigned investigator contacted the relationship manager for the Marisol Wolcott account. The relationship manager indicated that the account was established for personal use and that the expected activity profile did not include significant cash handling.

body: On April 20, 2023, Cortex Bank and Trust received a federal grand jury subpoena issued by the United States District Court for the Eastern District of New York. The subpoena demanded the production of all records relating to Anders Macallister, specifically referencing account 68-99803-2, for the period beginning June 15, 2023, and concluding on the date the subpoena was served. The subpoena requested signature cards, account opening documents, monthly statements, deposit tickets, withdrawal slips, cancelled checks, wire transfer records, and all correspondence related to the specified account. The bank's legal department, in coordination with the Financial Intelligence Unit, initiated the process of compiling the requested documentation. A complete production of the requested records was submitted to the designated Assistant United States Attorney on June 10, 2024. The subpoena did not specify the nature of the underlying investigation, nor did it request that the bank maintain the confidentiality of the request; however, standard bank procedures dictate that the existence of a grand jury subpoena is not disclosed to the customer.

The subpoena requested signature cards, account opening documents, monthly statements, deposit tickets, withdrawal slips, cancelled checks, wire transfer records, and all correspondence related to the specified account. The bank's legal department, in coordination with the Financial Intelligence Unit, initiated the process of compiling the requested documentation. A complete production of the requested records was submitted to the designated Assistant United States Attorney on June 10, 2024. The subpoena did not specify the nature of the underlying investigation, nor did it request that the bank maintain the confidentiality of the request; however, standard bank procedures dictate that the existence of a grand jury subpoena is not disclosed to the customer.

body:
A review of activity in Cortex Bank and Trust account 57-14456-1, maintained in the name of Summit Gate Produce Enterprises LLC, was initiated following a referral from the relationship manager on August 18, 2023. The referral cited customer assertions that an outbound funds transfer executed on August 17, 2023, was not authorized and that the intended recipient had not received the funds. The review period for this investigation was established as July 27, 2023, through June 6, 2024. The primary concern identified during the review was the unauthorized movement of funds out of a customer account via wire transfer, consistent with a wire fraud typology.

The fraud activity under review centers on an outbound wire transfer in the amount of $431,944.09. This transaction was initiated from the Summit Gate Produce Enterprises LLC account on August 17, 2023. The customer subsequently contacted Cortex Bank and Trust to report that the transfer was fraudulent, having been induced by deceptive instructions.

body: A review of the alert history for Summit Gate Produce Enterprises LLC, account 57-14456-1, identified two prior monitoring alerts generated during the review period. The analyst also contacted the relationship manager for Summit Gate Produce Enterprises LLC, who confirmed that the customer had recently discussed plans to expand their operations and required new equipment.

body:
The review period began on July 27, 2023, when Lakebridge Industrial Supply LLC received an invoice via email purportedly from Crescent Exports Partners LP, an established vendor. The invoice directed payment for industrial equipment to a new beneficiary account. The email originated from a domain that differed by a single character from the known vendor domain, a discrepancy not identified by Lakebridge Industrial Supply LLC personnel at the time of receipt.

On July 28, 2023, a representative of Lakebridge Industrial Supply LLC, acting on the instructions in the email, initiated an outbound wire transfer in the amount of $431,944.09. The transfer was executed minutes before the Cortex Bank and Trust daily wire cutoff time. The beneficiary named on the wire instructions did not match Crescent Exports Partners LP, the vendor that purportedly issued the invoice. The wire was processed by Cortex Bank and Trust and the funds were transmitted to the receiving institution.

On August 1, 2023, Lakebridge Industrial Supply LLC contacted Cortex Bank and Trust to report that Crescent Exports Partners LP had not received the anticipated payment.

The geographic profile of Beatriz Underhill and the transactions associated with Cortex Bank and Trust account 55-41591-2 present several elements that complicate the jurisdictional risk assessment for this review. The customer's residential address of record is located in a suburb of Chicago, Illinois, which is consistent with the location of the branch where the account was initially opened. However, a review of the transaction history during the review period ending June 6, 2024, reveals a pattern of activity that frequently originates from or is directed to locations outside of this primary geographic area, raising questions about the geographic nexus of the funds being moved.

A significant portion of the login activity for the online banking platform associated with account 55-41591-2 was traced to IP addresses geo-located in the Miami, Florida metropolitan area. This login activity was particularly concentrated around the dates of August 16, 2023, and August 17, 2023, which immediately preceded the execution of the fraudulent outbound wire on August 18, 2023.

A review of the digital session logs associated with account 55-41591-2, held by Beatriz Underhill, was conducted for the period surrounding the suspected fraudulent transfer. The analysis focused on identifying anomalies in access patterns, device usage, and authentication events that might indicate unauthorized access or account takeover, which would be inconsistent with the suspected typology of funds induced out of a customer account by deception.

The session data indicates that the online banking profile for Beatriz Underhill was accessed consistently from a single geographic region during the review period. The IP addresses associated with these logins resolved to an internet service provider in the same metropolitan area as the residential address on file for the customer. This pattern of access is consistent with a customer accessing their account from their home or local area. No logins were observed originating from foreign IP addresses or known anonymizing services, such as virtual private networks or Tor exit nodes, which are often associated with unauthorized access attempts.

body: Open-source research was conducted to establish the operational footprint and ownership structure of Lakebridge Industrial Supply LLC, the primary subject of this review. The entity maintains Cortex Bank and Trust account 79-44138-3, which was established on August 1, 2023. Corporate registry filings obtained from the Secretary of State for the jurisdiction of incorporation indicate that Lakebridge Industrial Supply LLC was formed on July 27, 2023, just four days prior to the account opening at Cortex Bank and Trust. The registered agent listed on the formation documents is a commercial registered agent service known to provide incorporation and mail forwarding services. The principal address provided to Cortex Bank and Trust during onboarding matches the address of this registered agent service, and open-source mapping applications confirm that this location is a retail mail center rather than a commercial or industrial facility. No other physical address for the business could be identified through public records or open-source searches.

body: On June 1, 2024, the reviewing analyst established that the principal balance of account 58-46375-9, held by Summit Gate Produce Enterprises LLC at another institution, had been commingled with funds controlled by a previously undisclosed counterparty. A review of wire transfer records confirmed that $981,952.31 was credited to the account on May 15, 2024, originating from Umberfield Management LLC. No business relationship between Summit Gate Produce Enterprises LLC and the originator could be substantiated through account opening documentation or subsequent customer outreach. The relationship manager noted that the customer had previously described their operations as entirely domestic, whereas the originator is a foreign-registered entity. The commingling of these funds with the customer's operating capital obscures the source of the balance and is inconsistent with the stated purpose of the account.

The transaction was subsequently blocked, and the matter escalated for further review.

The reviewing analyst noted the subpoena's receipt in the case file but could not determine the exact scope or focus of the external agency's investigation based on the information provided in the request.

Following the receipt of the subpoena, the reviewing analyst initiated a review of Obsidian Produce Corp.’s account activity within the timeframe specified by the external agency. This review identified several transactions involving Silverthorn Fabrication Inc. and Ironwood Trading Inc.

body:
This report details an investigation conducted by the Cortex Bank and Trust Financial Intelligence Unit regarding suspected wire fraud activity. The review period covers September 20, 2023 through July 4, 2024. The primary subject of this review is Hearthstone Marine Services Inc., an entity maintaining a commercial checking account, ending in 41-19402-1, at Cortex Bank and Trust. The investigation was initiated following a referral from the relationship manager assigned to the Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. account. The relationship manager reported that a representative of the subject company contacted Cortex Bank and Trust to report a suspected fraudulent funds transfer. The customer alleged that they were deceived into authorizing an outbound wire transfer to an unknown beneficiary. The activity reviewed began with the October 2023 outbound wire of $2,908,549.43 from the subject account.

The activity under review is consistent with a business email compromise scheme resulting in wire fraud. The typology typically involves the unauthorized access to, or spoofing of, corporate email accounts to intercept legitimate communications between a business and its vendors or clients.

body:
Following the identification of the fraudulent outbound wire transfer on October 5, 2023, Cortex Bank and Trust executed immediate containment measures on the account held by Hearthstone Marine Services Inc. The relationship manager initiated a total freeze on all outbound electronic funds transfers from account 41-19402-1, encompassing wire transfers, automated clearing house debits, and external account transfers. This restriction was implemented to prevent further capital flight while the investigation into the $2,908,549.43 disbursement proceeded. Concurrently, a stop payment order was applied to all pending, unpresented checks drawn on the account. The bank’s fraud operations unit contacted the receiving institution to request a recall of the funds; however, this request was only partially successful, resulting in the recovery of $584,317.62. The remaining balance of the transfer, totaling $2,324,231.81, represents the final loss sustained by the customer.

The reviewing analyst determined that the existing dual-approval control framework on the customer’s online banking profile had been compromised.

body: Following the identification of the suspected wire fraud activity involving the outbound transfer of $2,908,549.43, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated coordination efforts with relevant law enforcement agencies and other financial institutions. The subpoena requested all account records, transaction histories, wire transfer details, and know-your-customer documentation pertaining to Ulises Jankowski and account 55-71902-2, covering the period from September 20, 2023, through the date of the request. The subpoena specifically referenced an ongoing investigation into business email compromise and associated money laundering schemes. Cortex Bank and Trust complied with this subpoena, providing the requested documentation on November 15, 2023, through established secure electronic transmission channels. The provided records included the wire transfer authorization form, customer profile information, and correspondence between Ulises Jankowski and the relationship manager regarding the execution of the transfer.

body:

The escalation concerned discrepancies identified during the manual review of documentary trade collections and associated wire transfer instructions. The activity under review spanned the period from June 30, 2023, through May 17, 2024. During this timeframe, Emberline Marine Services Holdings Ltd. originated a series of outgoing international wire transfers and presented several letters of credit for negotiation. The aggregate value of the screened transactions subject to this review was $2,416,503.27. The transactions were primarily executed through the customer's commercial checking account, numbered 55-11207-1. The activity was identified as potentially indicative of sanctions evasion or exposure to a sanctioned jurisdiction, prompting a comprehensive Financial Intelligence Unit investigation.

The initial escalation occurred when trade operations staff reviewing a set of shipping documents associated with a letter of credit noted an irregularity in the routing of the underlying goods.

body: The determinative finding of the investigation into Emberline Marine Services Holdings Ltd. was established during the review of trade finance documentation supporting a series of letter of credit drawings. The reviewing analyst identified a pattern of discrepancies between the declared value of shipments and the subsequent payments routed through Cortex Bank and Trust. While the declared value of the shipment named in the trade documents was $570,360.71, subsequent analysis of the ultimate beneficiaries revealed a larger exposure. Specifically, the analyst determined that on April 25, 2024, a total of $2,173,619.78 was established as attributable to Gideon Bellweather, a party not previously disclosed in the transaction chain. This sum was ultimately credited to account 89-75825-9 at an outside institution. The failure to identify this exposure earlier was attributed to shipping documents being re-routed through a transshipment hub, obscuring the true destination and beneficiaries of the goods.

A core component of these obligations is the requirement to identify, monitor, and report suspicious activity. Cortex Bank and Trust policy mandates the reporting of transactions that involve funds derived from illegal activities, are intended to hide or disguise funds or assets derived from illegal activities, are designed to evade any requirements of the Bank Secrecy Act, or have no apparent business or lawful purpose. The bank's internal procedures dictate that activity must be evaluated against the regulatory threshold of $5,000 for suspicious activity reporting by a financial institution. The aggregate value of the screened transactions under review in this matter, totaling $2,416,503.27, substantially exceeds this mandatory reporting threshold.

The activity involving Alina Wolcott is evaluated against the bank's customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence policies.

Following the identification of the OFAC screening failure and the subsequent identification of the sanctioned counterparty, Cortex Bank and Trust undertook immediate remedial actions concerning the Bastion Metals Partners LP account, number 60-65686-2. The primary objective was to halt all further activity involving the sanctioned entity and to secure any funds related to the identified transactions while a comprehensive review of the customer relationship was conducted. The reviewing analyst recommended, and the Financial Intelligence Unit management approved, the immediate placement of a total block on the account. This block prevented any incoming or outgoing funds transfers, ACH transactions, and check clearings, effectively freezing the account balance.

Simultaneously, the bank acted to secure the funds associated with the specific transactions that had triggered the sanctions concern. The payment blocked and reported, which amounted to $101,549.00, was isolated and held in a suspense account pending further instructions from the Office of Foreign Assets Control. A second payment held pending resolution of the name match, totaling $59,754.00, was also segregated.

section: Law Enforcement Coordination and Information Sharing
body:
A formal request for information was received from a federal law enforcement agency on July 10, 2023, concerning Millpond Textiles Corp. and its account at Cortex Bank and Trust. The request sought transaction records, account opening documentation, and all correspondence related to wire transfers initiated by Millpond Textiles Corp. to foreign counterparties during the review period. The inquiry specifically referenced transactions involving Fieldstone Imports Trading Co. and Pinnacle Ridge Ventures Corp. Cortex Bank and Trust compiled the requested materials, encompassing account statements, wire transfer details, and know-your-customer files, and provided them to the requesting agency on July 14, 2023.

Subsequent to this initial request, Cortex Bank and Trust received a grand jury subpoena on July 20, 2023, expanding the scope of the inquiry. The subpoena demanded comprehensive records pertaining to Alina Wolcott, a signatory on the Millpond Textiles Corp. account, and her personal account at Cortex Bank and Trust.

body: The activity observed in the account held by Damaris Kirkpatrick, Cortex Bank and Trust account 20-19692-4, triggered review under the institution's obligations pursuant to the Bank Secrecy Act and its implementing regulations. The Bank Secrecy Act requires financial institutions to report suspicious transactions relevant to a possible violation of law or regulation. Suspicious Activity Report filings are required when transactions aggregate to $5,000 or more and the institution knows, suspects, or has reason to suspect that the transaction involves funds derived from illegal activities, is designed to evade any requirements of the Bank Secrecy Act, or has no business or apparent lawful purpose. The activity identified in the Kirkpatrick account meets the quantitative threshold for reporting, as the aggregate amount withdrawn during the review period was $1,428,517.36, well exceeding the $5,000 requirement. The qualitative assessment of the activity, as detailed in the transaction analysis sections, forms the basis for evaluating the suspicion element of the reporting requirement.

body: The activity described in this report, specifically regarding the account held by Séverin Castellanos, was reviewed in accordance with Cortex Bank and Trust's obligations under the Bank Secrecy Act and related anti-money laundering regulations. The Bank Secrecy Act requires financial institutions to report suspicious activity that might signal criminal activity, including money laundering, tax evasion, or other financial crimes. This obligation is central to the bank's role in safeguarding the financial system and ensuring that its services are not utilized for illicit purposes. A key component of this regulatory framework is the requirement to identify and report transactions that appear designed to evade reporting requirements, a practice commonly known as structuring. Structuring involves breaking down larger, reportable transactions into smaller, sub-threshold amounts to avoid triggering the filing of a Currency Transaction Report. The regulatory threshold for filing a Currency Transaction Report is established at $10,000 in cash transactions, either deposited or withdrawn, by or on behalf of the same person on a single business day.

Following the completion of the investigation into Cedarline Exports Enterprises LLC, account 88-53482-2, the Cortex Bank and Trust Financial Intelligence Unit initiated a series of remediation actions designed to mitigate the risks associated with the observed cash activity. The volume of the aggregate cash deposits during the review period, totaling $899,468.70, combined with the pattern of branch rotation within a single business day and the documented customer questions about reporting thresholds at the teller line, necessitated immediate intervention to limit the potential for further structuring and to ensure the bank's compliance with Bank Secrecy Act obligations. body: The activity identified in the account held by Valentina Grimaldi requires review against Cortex Bank and Trust policies governing the detection and reporting of suspected wire fraud. The activity is evaluated in the context of the Bank Secrecy Act and its implementing regulations, which mandate the filing of a Suspicious Activity Report when a financial institution detects a known or suspected violation of federal law, a suspicious transaction related to a money laundering activity, or a violation of the Bank Secrecy Act. body:

This request sought further clarification regarding the specific individuals authorized to initiate wire transfers on behalf of Greystone Ventures Corp.

body:

body: The activity observed in the account held by Delia Dalrymple, acting in her capacity as an authorized signer or beneficial owner, is evaluated under the framework established by the Bank Secrecy Act and its implementing regulations, specifically those concerning anti-money laundering program requirements and customer due diligence. The Bank Secrecy Act requires financial institutions to establish and maintain procedures reasonably designed to identify and verify the identity of their customers. This obligation, further codified in the customer identification program rules, mandates that institutions collect identifying information, verify that information to a reasonable belief of the customer's true identity, and maintain records of the verification process. The regulations also require institutions to understand the nature and purpose of customer relationships to develop a customer risk profile and to conduct ongoing monitoring to identify and report suspicious transactions. Furthermore, the beneficial ownership rule necessitates the collection and verification of identifying information for individuals who own or control legal entity customers.

body:

The agency also requested records pertaining to any wire transfers originating from or destined for the account, with a particular focus on transactions involving foreign jurisdictions.

In response to the written request, Cortex Bank and Trust compiled the requested records. The bank provided the account opening documents, which indicated that the account was established on September 14, 2023. The bank also provided transaction records for the requested period, which documented the opening deposit on September 15, 2023.

body:

The purpose of this research was to identify any adverse media, civil litigation, regulatory actions, or significant public records that might provide context for the unusual activity observed in account 49-96766-2 during the review period. Searches utilized variations of the subject's name, known addresses, and dates of birth as search criteria.

Initial queries returned a substantial volume of results, requiring significant effort to differentiate confirmed matches from false positives. A primary area of focus was corporate registry filings, given the nature of the counterparties involved in the broader investigation. A search of state corporate registries in the jurisdictions associated with Ashworth’s known addresses yielded a confirmed match. Ashworth is listed as a managing member of Umberfield Machinery Group LLC. This entity was registered in 2018. The business address provided for Umberfield Machinery Group LLC matches the primary residential address on file for Ashworth at Cortex Bank and Trust.

body:
On December 11, 2023, the relationship manager for Rafferty Duvall, the primary accountholder for Cortex Bank and Trust account 16-61489-5, requested a meeting with the customer. The relationship manager initiated this contact following a review of recent account activity that appeared inconsistent with the customer's historical transaction patterns, which had remained largely unchanged for several decades. The interview was conducted in person at the branch. The customer was accompanied by Dashiell Castellanos, who had been added as a joint signer to the account in late November 2023.

During the interview, the relationship manager inquired about the recent withdrawals from the account. The relationship manager noted that the customer appeared hesitant and deferred to the accompanying party, Dashiell Castellanos, to answer questions regarding the transactions. Dashiell Castellanos stated that the funds were being used to pay for unspecified medical expenses and home repairs. When pressed for details or documentation regarding these expenses, the accompanying party became defensive and stated that the customer was entitled to use the funds as desired.

body: The determinative finding of this review is that the subject Kirsten Larkspur was accompanied into the branch by an unidentified male who directed the branch teller to transfer $205,138.84 to an external account held by Ironwood Marine Services Group LLC. The subject appeared disoriented and deferred to the accompanying party when asked the purpose of the transfer, stating only that it was for an investment. The branch teller declined the transfer, noting the transaction was uncharacteristic for the subject and the accompanying party was aggressive. A review of account activity identified that the subject had added an authorized signer to account 33-13983-1 weeks prior to this event. On September 26, 2024, the newly authorized signer initiated a wire transfer for a low six-figure sum to external account 59-84252-9, which is held by the same entity that the accompanying party had attempted to fund.

body: The activity observed in the account of Dashiell Castellanos, specifically account 80-26926-4, is subject to the reporting obligations established under the Bank Secrecy Act and its implementing regulations, particularly those concerning the filing of Suspicious Activity Reports by depository institutions. The regulatory framework requires Cortex Bank and Trust to report any transaction conducted or attempted by, at, or through the bank if the transaction involves or aggregates to at least the $5,000 threshold and the bank knows, suspects, or has reason to suspect that the transaction involves funds derived from illegal activities or is intended or conducted in order to hide or disguise funds or assets derived from illegal activities. The activity in the Castellanos account, which aggregated to $499,911.45 in withdrawals during the review period, significantly exceeds the $5,000 reporting threshold, thereby triggering the regulatory requirement for evaluation and potential reporting.

body: The investigation into the activity within the account of Kirsten Larkspur was initiated following a referral from the branch manager, who documented concerns regarding a change in account behavior and the influence of an accompanying party during in-person transactions. The referral noted that the customer, who had maintained a consistent transaction profile for several decades, executed a series of withdrawals that appeared uncharacteristic. The branch manager reported that during these transactions, an accompanying party directed the customer's actions and answered questions on their behalf. The referral specifically cited three withdrawals executed on consecutive days, totaling a low five-figure sum, which were directed by the accompanying party. The first withdrawal, executed on December 21, 2023, was for $2,725.55. A second withdrawal for $1,896.00 occurred on December 22, 2023, and a third withdrawal for $4,380.03 was processed on December 26, 2023. The branch manager observed that the customer appeared confused when asked about the purpose of the transactions and deferred to the accompanying party for explanation.

body: Following the identification of the anomalous withdrawal pattern in the account held by Beatriz Ashworth, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated protective measures to secure the remaining funds and mitigate further potential elder financial exploitation. The aggregate amount withdrawn during the review period totaled $499,911.45. Upon review of the account activity on December 21, 2023, the reviewing analyst placed a temporary, system-level hold on all outbound transfers from the subject account. This initial action prevented any further electronic funds transfers, automated clearing house debits, or wire transfers from being executed. This hold was applied to ensure the remaining balance of $167,229.11 was secured while a more comprehensive investigation could be completed. The temporary hold was subsequently converted to a permanent outbound restriction on December 22, 2023, after the reviewing analyst confirmed the transaction pattern was inconsistent with the subject’s historical activity. This permanent restriction blocked all automated outgoing transactions, including bill pay services and pre-authorized debits, effectively freezing the account's liquidity for external transfers.

section: Law Enforcement Coordination and Information Sharing
body:
Cortex Bank and Trust received a formal written request for information regarding Rafferty Calloway and account 39-87741-3 on December 11, 2023. The request originated from a regional task force investigating organized financial crime affecting elderly populations. The task force cited ongoing investigations involving several related individuals and entities, although the specific scope of the inquiry concerning Rafferty Calloway was not detailed in the initial correspondence. The request sought account records, transaction histories, and any available documentation identifying authorized signers or recent changes to account mandates for the period beginning December 6, 2023. Cortex Bank and Trust acknowledged receipt of the request on December 15, 2023, and commenced a review of the specified records to fulfill the production requirements.

In response to the written request, Cortex Bank and Trust provided responsive documents on December 21, 2023. The production included statements for account 39-87741-3 covering the requested period, copies of signature cards, and records documenting the addition of a joint signer shortly before the commencement of the review period.

body: Cortex Bank and Trust is filing this report because the activity described above is consistent with an older accountholder's funds being moved by or for someone who has acquired influence over the account and no legitimate business purpose was identified for it. The determination rests on the key finding recorded above. The relationship has been placed under enhanced monitoring, the monitoring scenarios that generated the underlying alerts have been retuned for this customer segment, and a relationship review has been scheduled. Supporting documentation is retained in internal case file FIU-2024-1740 and is available to law enforcement on request.
